children: S&P 500 earnings moved into high gear this week, with 24 major companies reporting across the Financials, Health Care, Industrials, Consumer, and Real Estate sectors. Heavyweights in banking, asset management, and healthcare set early benchmarks for net interest income, capital markets activity, and consumer spending health.
Out of the 24 companies reporting, 20 exceeded EPS expectations, while 3 fell short and 1 matched estimates. Notably, 23 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth.
Out of the 24 companies reporting, 15 exceeded revenue expectations, while 9 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, 20 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.
Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

Diluted EPS of $1.87 beat the $1.85 forecast, bolstered by consumer (+5% to $10.66B), commercial (+6% to $3.24B), and wealth management (+12% to $4.10B) growth. Strong services and wealth growth alongside $17.0B in NII prompted Citi to raise its FY26 ex-markets NII growth guidance to mid-to-high 6% and boost its ROTCE target to >11%.

Backed by strong deposit growth, USB raised its FY26 revenue growth outlook to 8%–9% and expanded its operating leverage target to ~300 bps.
